text:
alice: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need a single place for the remediation TODOs and a clear escalation ladder. Can we agree owners and short timelines? Goal: have updated playbook + owners by next Tue EOD. :calendar:
ben: I can take ownership of the cache eviction remediation. Will add the exact commands and a test checklist. ETA Mon noon.
clara: I'll own the escalation ladder updates (when to page infra vs oncall). I'll propose thresholds.
dave: adding a draft triage checklist now, keeping it minimal so oncall can run it fast.
ben: tentative checklist snippet:
```
1) Confirm latency spike in prod: grafana -> inference/latency, look at p95/p99
2) Check model routing: curl -sS "http://infra-api/services/routing?model=active"
3) Inspect KV cache hit ratio: curl -s http://cache-metrics/internal | jq .hit_rate
4) If hit_rate < 65%, toggle prefix-caching fallback: POST /admin/cache/fallback
```
alice: nice. Also add the concrete `kubectl` logs commands — those saved a TON during yesterday's run.
dave: putting this in too:
```
# tail runtime logs for inference pods
kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=inference -c runtime --tail=500
# check recent restarts
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=inference -o wide | grep CrashLoop
```
clara: For escalation ladder, propose: pager to infra on P1 if error-rate > 5% for 5m OR p99 latency > 2s for 10m. Otherwise, notify oncall via Slack and create incident. Thoughts?
ben: sounds reasonable. For model fallback, we should define exactly which model variants to swap to and how to roll back. I'll add a one-liner command to trigger variant swap in the runbook.
alice: include rollback criteria: error-rate back to baseline and p99 below target for 10 consecutive minutes. Also add who signs off on rollback (service owner).
incident-bot: Reminder: please add owners in the postmortem tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1234 — due by 2025-06-03 17:00 UTC.
clara: I'll add the oncall paging matrix and callout for legal/security for customer-impact incidents.
dave: noting recurring pattern from the postmortems: "cache warmup thrash" during traffic bursts. Action: add automated warmup and a metric to detect warmup phase.
ben: for the warmup script, adding example curl to prime prefix cache:
```
# prime cache for top prefixes from daily traffic sample
python tools/prime_cache.py --prefix-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt --concurrency 5
```
alice: good. For tracking status, let's use the postmortem issue with subtasks per remediation and weekly check-ins until closed. I'll create the subtasks now and assign.
ben: I'll attach a short test plan for the cache change (staging run + canary).
clara: once I finish the ladder I'll post in #oncall with a short summary and link.
dave: Can someone add the quick triage commands as pinned items in the incident runbook? That helped the SRE team yesterday.
alice: I'll pin them and mark a note about expected timelines for each action (5m quick checks, 30m mitigation, 4h remediation).
incident-bot: Assigned tasks created: INF-2345 (cache remediation) -> ben, INF-2346 (escalation ladder) -> clara, INF-2347 (triage checklist) -> dave. Deadlines set.
ben: I'll open a draft PR for the playbook updates this afternoon. Requesting review from @alice and @clara.
clara: will review. Also adding a small flowchart for the ladder so new oncall can follow it easily.
dave: adding a short runbook card for the release playbook to avoid model-variant swaps during deployments.
alice: thanks team — let's aim to close the postmortem action items by next Wednesday and sync in the incidents retro. :thumbsup:
